accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.abstract: Accessible user interfaces empower everyone to have a great experience with your app or game.

action-sheets.title: Action sheets
action-sheets.abstract: An action sheet is a modal view that presents choices related to an action people initiate.

activity-views.title: Activity views
activity-views.abstract: An activity view — often called a *share sheet* — presents a range of tasks that people can perform in the current context.

airplay.title: AirPlay
airplay.abstract: AirPlay lets people stream media content wirelessly from iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and tvOS devices to Apple TV, HomePod, and TVs and speakers that support AirPlay.

alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.abstract: An alert gives people critical information they need right away.

app-clips.title: App Clips
app-clips.abstract: An App Clip is a lightweight version of your app or game that provides an on-the-go or demo experience that’s instantly available.
headings: Creating content for an App Clip card

app-icons.title: App icons
app-icons.abstract: A unique, memorable icon expresses your app’s or game’s purpose and personality and helps people recognize it at a glance.

app-shortcuts.title: App Shortcuts
app-shortcuts.abstract: An App Shortcut gives people access to your app’s key functions or content throughout the system.

apple-in-app-purchase.title: Apple In-App Purchase
apple-in-app-purchase.abstract: People can use Apple In-App Purchase to pay for digital goods and services, like premium content and subscriptions, securely within your app.

apple-pay.title: Apple Pay
apple-pay.abstract: Apple Pay is a secure, easy way to make payments for physical goods and services, donations, and subscriptions in apps and in any browser.

apple-pencil-and-scribble.title: Apple Pencil and Scribble
apple-pencil-and-scribble.abstract: Apple Pencil helps make drawing, handwriting, and marking effortless and natural, in addition to performing well as a pointer and UI interaction tool.

augmented-reality.title: Augmented reality
augmented-reality.abstract: Augmented reality (or AR) lets you deliver immersive, engaging experiences that seamlessly blend virtual objects with the real world.

boxes.title: Boxes
boxes.abstract: A box creates a visually distinct group of logically related information and components.

branding.title: Branding
branding.abstract: Apps and games express their unique brand identity in ways that make them instantly recognizable while feeling at home on the platform and giving people a consistent experience.

buttons.title: Buttons
buttons.abstract: A button initiates an instantaneous action.

charting-data.title: Charting data
charting-data.abstract: Presenting data in a chart can help you communicate information with clarity and appeal.

charts.title: Charts
charts.abstract: Organize data in a chart to communicate information with clarity and visual appeal.
headings: Enhancing the accessibility of a chart

collaboration-and-sharing.title: Collaboration and sharing
collaboration-and-sharing.abstract: Great collaboration and sharing experiences are simple and responsive, letting people engage with the content while communicating effectively with others.

collections.title: Collections
collections.abstract: A collection manages an ordered set of content and presents it in a customizable and highly visual layout.

color-wells.title: Color wells
color-wells.abstract: A color well lets people adjust the color of text, shapes, guides, and other onscreen elements.

color.title: Color
color.abstract: Judicious use of color can enhance communication, evoke your brand, provide visual continuity, communicate status and feedback, and help people understand information.

column-views.title: Column views
column-views.abstract: A column view — also called a *browser* — lets people view and navigate a data hierarchy using a series of vertical columns.

combo-boxes.title: Combo boxes
combo-boxes.abstract: A combo box combines a text field with a pull-down button in a single control.

context-menus.title: Context menus
context-menus.abstract: A context menu provides access to functionality that’s directly related to an item, without cluttering the interface.

controls.title: Controls
controls.abstract: A control provides quick access to a feature of your app from Control Center, the Lock Screen, or the Action button.
headings: Camera experiences on a locked device

dark-mode.title: Dark Mode
dark-mode.abstract: Dark Mode is a systemwide appearance setting that uses a dark color palette to provide a comfortable viewing experience tailored for low-light environments.

design-principles.title: Design principles
design-principles.abstract: Explore fundamental principles that guide design across Apple platforms.

designing-for-games.title: Designing for games
designing-for-games.abstract: When people play your game on an Apple device, they dive into the world you designed while relying on the platform features they love.

designing-for-ios.title: Designing for iOS
designing-for-ios.abstract: People depend on their iPhone to help them stay connected, play games, view media, accomplish tasks, and track personal data in any location and while on the go.

designing-for-ipados.title: Designing for iPadOS
designing-for-ipados.abstract: People value the power, mobility, and flexibility of iPad as they enjoy media, play games, perform detailed productivity tasks, and bring their creations to life.

designing-for-iphone-duo.title: Designing for iPhone Duo
designing-for-iphone-duo.abstract: An app designed for iPhone Duo adapts seamlessly to both displays, providing a continuous experience as the device opens and closes.

designing-for-macos.title: Designing for macOS
designing-for-macos.abstract: People rely on the power, spaciousness, and flexibility of a Mac as they perform in-depth productivity tasks, view media or content, and play games, often using several apps at once.

disclosure-controls.title: Disclosure controls
disclosure-controls.abstract: Disclosure controls reveal and hide information and functionality related to specific controls or views.

dock-menus.title: Dock menus
dock-menus.abstract: On a Mac, people can secondary click an app’s or game’s icon in the Dock to reveal a Dock menu, which presents both system-provided and custom items.

drag-and-drop.title: Drag and drop
drag-and-drop.abstract: Using drag and drop, people can move or duplicate selected photos, text, and other content by dragging the selection from one location to another.

edit-menus.title: Edit menus
edit-menus.abstract: An edit menu lets people make changes to selected content in the current view, in addition to offering related commands like Copy, Select, Translate, and Look Up.

entering-data.title: Entering data
entering-data.abstract: When you need information from people, design ways that make it easy for them to provide it without making mistakes.

feedback.title: Feedback
feedback.abstract: Feedback helps people know what’s happening, discover what they can do next, understand the results of actions, and avoid mistakes.

file-management.title: File management
file-management.abstract: Some apps can support documents and files that people expect to manage throughout the system.

focus-and-selection.title: Focus and selection
focus-and-selection.abstract: Focus helps people visually confirm the object that their interaction targets.

game-controls.title: Game controls
game-controls.abstract: Precise, intuitive game controls enhance gameplay and can increase a player’s immersion in the game.

gauges.title: Gauges
gauges.abstract: A gauge displays a specific numerical value within a range of values.

generative-ai.title: Generative AI
generative-ai.abstract: Generative AI empowers you to enhance your app or game with dynamic content and offer intelligent features that unlock new levels of creativity, connection, and productivity.

gestures.title: Gestures
gestures.abstract: A gesture is a physical motion that a person uses to directly affect an object in an app or game on their device.
headings: macOS trackpad and touch display gestures

going-full-screen.title: Going full screen
going-full-screen.abstract: iPhone, iPad, and Mac offer full-screen modes that let people expand a window to fill the screen, hiding system controls and providing a distraction-free environment.

gyro-and-accelerometer.title: Gyroscope and accelerometer
gyro-and-accelerometer.abstract: On-device gyroscopes and accelerometers can supply data about a device’s movement in the physical world.

home-screen-quick-actions.title: Home Screen quick actions
home-screen-quick-actions.abstract: Home Screen quick actions give people a way to perform app-specific actions from the Home Screen.

icloud.title: iCloud
icloud.abstract: iCloud is a service that lets people seamlessly access the content they care about — photos, videos, documents, and more — from any device, without performing explicit synchronization.

icons.title: Icons
icons.abstract: An effective icon is a graphic asset that expresses a single concept in ways people instantly understand.

image-views.title: Image views
image-views.abstract: An image view displays a single image — or in some cases, an animated sequence of images — on a transparent or opaque background.

image-wells.title: Image wells
image-wells.abstract: An image well is an editable version of an image view.

images.title: Images
images.abstract: To make sure your artwork looks great on all devices you support, learn how the system displays content and how to deliver art at the appropriate scale factors.

inclusion.title: Inclusion
inclusion.abstract: Inclusive apps and games put people first by prioritizing respectful communication and presenting content and functionality in ways that everyone can access and understand.

keyboards.title: Keyboards
keyboards.abstract: A physical keyboard can be an essential input device for entering text, playing games, controlling apps, and more.

labels.title: Labels
labels.abstract: A label is a static piece of text that people can read and often copy, but not edit.

launching.title: Launching
launching.abstract: A streamlined launch experience helps people start using your app or game immediately.

layout.title: Layout
layout.abstract: A consistent layout that adapts across display sizes, orientations, and multitasking configurations helps people understand and enjoy your app or game on all their devices.

liquid-glass.title: Liquid Glass
liquid-glass.abstract: Liquid Glass is the dynamic, translucent material Apple introduced in 2025 for the layer of controls and navigation that floats above an app's content. Use this guide whenever a design uses glass, blur, or frosted surfaces, whether it ships on Apple platforms or imitates the look elsewhere.

lists-and-tables.title: Lists and tables
lists-and-tables.abstract: Lists and tables present data in one or more columns of rows.

live-activities.title: Live Activities
live-activities.abstract: A Live Activity lets people track the progress of an activity, event, or task at a glance.
headings: Adding transitions and animating content updates
Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity

live-viewing-apps.title: Live-viewing apps
live-viewing-apps.abstract: As you design a live-viewing app, prioritize the content and create fun, fluid interactions that encourage immersion in the live-viewing experience.

loading.title: Loading
loading.abstract: The best content-loading experience finishes before people become aware of it.

machine-learning.title: Machine learning
machine-learning.abstract: Machine learning enables apps and games to learn from data and usage patterns, letting you improve existing experiences and create engaging new ones.
headings: The role of machine learning in your app

managing-accounts.title: Managing accounts
managing-accounts.abstract: When it doesn’t create an unnecessary barrier to your experience, an account can be a convenient way for people to access their content and track personal details.

managing-notifications.title: Managing notifications
managing-notifications.abstract: Notifications can give people timely and important information, whether the device is locked or in use.

maps.title: Maps
maps.abstract: A map displays outdoor or indoor geographical data in your app or on your website.
headings: Displaying place cards in a map
Adding place cards outside of a map

materials.title: Materials
materials.abstract: A material is a visual effect that creates a sense of depth, layering, and hierarchy between foreground and background elements.

menus.title: Menus
menus.abstract: A menu reveals its options when people interact with it, making it a space-efficient way to present commands in your app or game.

modality.title: Modality
modality.abstract: Modality is a design technique that presents content in a separate, dedicated mode that prevents interaction with the parent view and requires an explicit action to dismiss.

motion.title: Motion
motion.abstract: Beautiful, fluid motions bring the interface to life, conveying status, providing feedback and instruction, and enriching the visual experience of your app or game.

multitasking.title: Multitasking
multitasking.abstract: Multitasking lets people switch quickly from one app to another, performing tasks in each.

nfc.title: NFC
nfc.abstract: Near-field communication (NFC) allows devices within a few centimeters of each other to exchange information wirelessly.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.abstract: A notification gives people timely, high-value information they can understand at a glance.

offering-help.title: Offering help
offering-help.abstract: Although the most effective experiences are approachable and intuitive, you can provide contextual help when necessary.

onboarding.title: Onboarding
onboarding.abstract: Onboarding can help people get a quick start using your app or game.

outline-views.title: Outline views
outline-views.abstract: An outline view presents hierarchical data in a scrolling list of cells that are organized into columns and rows.

page-controls.title: Page controls
page-controls.abstract: A page control displays a row of indicator images, each of which represents a page in a flat list.

panels.title: Panels
panels.abstract: In a macOS app, a panel typically floats above other open windows providing supplementary controls, options, or information related to the active window or current selection.

path-controls.title: Path controls
path-controls.abstract: A path control shows the file system path of a selected file or folder.

pickers.title: Pickers
pickers.abstract: A picker displays one or more scrollable lists of distinct values that people can choose from.

playing-audio.title: Playing audio
playing-audio.abstract: People expect rich audio experiences that automatically adjust when the context changes on the device.

playing-haptics.title: Playing haptics
playing-haptics.abstract: Playing haptics can engage people’s sense of touch and bring their familiarity with the physical world into your app or game.

playing-video.title: Playing video
playing-video.abstract: People expect to enjoy rich video experiences on their devices, regardless of the app or game they’re using.

pointing-devices.title: Pointing devices
pointing-devices.abstract: People can use a pointing device like a trackpad or mouse to navigate the interface and initiate actions.

pop-up-buttons.title: Pop-up buttons
pop-up-buttons.abstract: A pop-up button displays a menu of mutually exclusive options.

popovers.title: Popovers
popovers.abstract: A popover is a transient view that appears above other content when people click or tap a control or interactive area.

printing.title: Printing
printing.abstract: An iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or visionOS app can integrate system-provided print functionality when it makes sense, presenting custom printer- and document-specific options if necessary.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.abstract: Privacy is paramount: it’s critical to be transparent about the privacy-related data and resources you require and essential to protect the data people allow you to access.

progress-indicators.title: Progress indicators
progress-indicators.abstract: Progress indicators let people know that your app isn’t stalled while it loads content or performs lengthy operations.

pull-down-buttons.title: Pull-down buttons
pull-down-buttons.abstract: A pull-down button displays a menu of items or actions that directly relate to the button’s purpose.

rating-indicators.title: Rating indicators
rating-indicators.abstract: A rating indicator uses a series of horizontally arranged graphical symbols — by default, stars — to communicate a ranking level.

ratings-and-reviews.title: Ratings and reviews
ratings-and-reviews.abstract: People often view the ratings and reviews for an app or game before they download it.

right-to-left.title: Right to left
right-to-left.abstract: Support right-to-left languages like Arabic and Hebrew by reversing your interface as needed to match the reading direction of the related scripts.

scroll-views.title: Scroll views
scroll-views.abstract: A scroll view lets people view content that’s larger than the view’s boundaries by moving the content vertically or horizontally.

search-fields.title: Search fields
search-fields.abstract: A search field lets people search a collection of content for specific terms they enter.

searching.title: Searching
searching.abstract: People use various search techniques to find content on their device, within an app, and within a document or file.

segmented-controls.title: Segmented controls
segmented-controls.abstract: A segmented control is a linear set of two or more segments, each of which functions as a button.

settings.title: Settings
settings.abstract: People expect apps and games to just work, but they also appreciate having ways to customize the experience to fit their needs.

sf-symbols.title: SF Symbols
sf-symbols.abstract: SF Symbols provides thousands of consistent, highly configurable symbols that integrate seamlessly with the San Francisco system font, automatically aligning with text in all weights and sizes.

sheets.title: Sheets
sheets.abstract: A sheet helps people perform a scoped task that’s closely related to their current context.

sidebars.title: Sidebars
sidebars.abstract: A sidebar appears on the leading side of a view and lets people navigate between areas of your app or top-level collections of content, like folders and playlists.

sign-in-with-apple.title: Sign in with Apple
sign-in-with-apple.abstract: Sign in with Apple provides a fast, private way to sign into apps and websites, giving people a consistent experience they can trust and the convenience of not having to remember multiple accounts and passwords.
headings: Creating a custom Sign in with Apple button
Custom buttons with a logo and text

siri.title: Siri
siri.abstract: People use Siri to help them with the things they need to find, know, or do every day.
headings: Getting your app to work with Siri
Customizing your app’s experience with Siri

sliders.title: Sliders
sliders.abstract: A slider is a horizontal track with a control, called a thumb, that people can adjust between a minimum and maximum value.

snippets.title: Snippets
snippets.abstract: When someone performs a task with Siri or an App Shortcut, a snippet shows the result or asks for confirmation.

split-views.title: Split views
split-views.abstract: A split view manages the presentation of multiple adjacent panes of content, each of which can contain a variety of components, including tables, collections, images, and custom views.

status-bars.title: Status bars
status-bars.abstract: A status bar appears along the upper edge of the screen and displays information about the device’s current state, like the time, cellular carrier, and battery level.

steppers.title: Steppers
steppers.abstract: A stepper is a two-segment control that people use to increase or decrease an incremental value.

tab-bars.title: Tab bars
tab-bars.abstract: A tab bar lets people navigate between top-level sections of your app.

tab-views.title: Tab views
tab-views.abstract: A tab view presents multiple mutually exclusive panes of content in the same area, which people can switch between using a tabbed control.

text-fields.title: Text fields
text-fields.abstract: A text field is a rectangular area in which people enter or edit small, specific pieces of text.

text-views.title: Text views
text-views.abstract: A text view displays multiline, styled text content, which can optionally be editable.

the-menu-bar.title: The menu bar
the-menu-bar.abstract: On a Mac or an iPad, the menu bar at the top of the screen displays the top-level menus in your app or game.

toggles.title: Toggles
toggles.abstract: A toggle lets people choose between a pair of opposing states, like on and off, using a different appearance to indicate each state.

token-fields.title: Token fields
token-fields.abstract: A token field is a type of text field that can convert text into *tokens* that are easy to select and manipulate.

toolbars.title: Toolbars
toolbars.abstract: A toolbar provides convenient access to frequently used commands, controls, navigation, and search.

typography.title: Typography
typography.abstract: Your typographic choices can help you display legible text, convey an information hierarchy, communicate important content, and express your brand or style.
headings: iOS, iPadOS larger accessibility type sizes

undo-and-redo.title: Undo and redo
undo-and-redo.abstract: Undo and redo gives people easy ways to reverse many types of actions, which can also help people explore and experiment safely as they learn a new interface or task.

virtual-keyboards.title: Virtual keyboards
virtual-keyboards.abstract: On devices without physical keyboards, the system offers various types of virtual keyboards people can use to enter data.

voiceover.title: VoiceOver
voiceover.abstract: VoiceOver is a screen reader that lets people experience your app’s interface without needing to see the screen.

web-views.title: Web views
web-views.abstract: A web view loads and displays rich web content, such as embedded HTML and websites, directly within your app.

widgets.title: Widgets
widgets.abstract: A widget provides quick access to essential information and focused interactions from your app or game in additional contexts.

windows.title: Windows
windows.abstract: A window presents UI views and components in your app or game.

writing.title: Writing
writing.abstract: The words you choose within your app are an essential part of its user experience.
